command: SSH isolated-/tmp exact-wheel install and diagnostics on Ubuntu 22.04 with the host real npm/Python command inventory retained
decisions: The transferred exact wheel SHA-256 was verified as 5589a97a2a41136068458c6d4c6797ac81c62a004e1aabf9ad0846900951a24d before local installation.
The wheel was installed with uv into an isolated /tmp tool root and reported jarn 1.0.4 on Ubuntu 22.04/glibc 2.35.

A customized schema-0 config in the isolated HOME migrated to schema 3 with one byte-identical backup, preserved its operator comment, custom header, timeout, routing, permission, theme, and log level, and remained current on a second offline doctor run.
The host inventory retained its real user-space, nvm/npm, and global commands; the real user config and both fingerprinted executable paths remained byte-identical after the isolated UAT.
Doctor output stayed machine-readable and network.checked=false; no authentication ceremony or provider request was run.
result: The exact v1.0.4 wheel ran on Ubuntu 22.04/glibc 2.35 in an isolated tool root, migrated a customized legacy config transactionally, produced bounded offline diagnostics, and left every real host command/config fingerprint unchanged.
limitations: This is exact-wheel and source-installer evidence before an immutable v1.0.4 tag exists; it does not claim a public release URL, release binary, or candidate commit.
Binary glibc-fallback and shell-activation behavior remains covered by exact v1.0.4 source tests and must be repeated by the protected tagged release workflow before promotion.
The UAT used an existing disposable SSH account with an isolated /tmp HOME rather than provisioning a new operating-system user.
